title: Duplicating twice does not make two Rectangle copy
goal: Duplicating a layer twice leaves two layers with exactly the same name, so the layers list shows the same row twice and you have to click each one to tell them apart. A copy should take a free name the way a newly drawn layer now does.
notes: Split out of a-second-rectangle-is-not-called-rectangle (2026-09-03). New layers are numbered in PhotonzDocument.uniquelyNamed, called from addLayer/addLayerOnFrame. Duplicate does not go through those: Document.duplicateLayers, duplicateLayers(movingCopiesTo:) and duplicateLayer insert copies straight into the sibling list inside a walk, so the taken-name set is mid-flight and the rename has to happen in a pass after the walk. Layer.duplicated mints the name (name + " copy"), so the policy question is whether the second copy reads "Rectangle copy 2" or takes the next plain number.
acceptance: Duplicating one layer twice gives two differently named copies
A copy of a layer a person named keeps that person name as its base
Undo puts the names back as they were
